title: 1980s Olympic Distance: They Swapped Events
description: Two Brits, a Moscow swap, a barefoot tangle in L.A., and a Moroccan 10K—five steps into 1980s Olympic distance.
imageHint: The classic oval track with distinctive lane markings where athletic legends were made

questions.question: At the boycotted 1980 Moscow Games, which Brit won the men's 800m—the race Seb Coe later called the worst of his life?
questions.explanation: Coe was the world-record favorite and took silver. British fans got the first half of a lifelong argument: who was better, and who stole whose race?

questions.question: Six days after Ovett beat him at 800m, Coe redeemed himself by winning which event in Moscow—Ovett's specialty?
questions.explanation: They swapped events: Ovett took Coe's 800, Coe took Ovett's 1500. Jürgen Straub of East Germany took silver; Ovett settled for bronze. Coe remains the only man to win Olympic 1500m gold twice.

questions.question: After his Moscow 1500m gold, Coe defended that title at which 1984 Games, outsprinting favorite Steve Cram on the final turn?
questions.explanation: He pulled away on the final bend and won by about six meters. He also took 800m silver again—this time behind Brazil's Joaquim Cruz. Two Games, two 1500 golds.

questions.question: At those same Los Angeles Games, Mary Decker and barefoot Zola Budd tangled in the women's 3000m—and which Romanian stayed clear for gold?
questions.explanation: Decker clipped Budd and fell hard. Budd, running barefoot for Britain, finished seventh; Decker did not finish. Puică never broke stride—the race everyone remembers for the fall, not the winner.

questions.question: Four years after Puică's Los Angeles gold, which Moroccan—not the favorite Aouita—set an Olympic record to win the men's 10,000m in Seoul?
questions.explanation: His 27:21.44 held off Italy's Salvatore Antibo. Aouita, Morocco's other star that Games, took 800m bronze instead. Another decade, another distance surprise.

easterEgg.title: They swapped events
easterEgg.text: In Moscow, each Brit won the other's specialty: Ovett took Coe's 800m, Coe took Ovett's 1500m. Two golds for Britain, one lifelong pub argument, and Coe later became an IOC powerbroker who helped bring the Olympics to London.
